To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
monitoring effectiveness is highly dependent on the underlying ecological processes and the budgetary and observational conditions under which monitoring takes place.

In summary, our research is concerned with
how to detect trends under uncertainty and what the underlying processes are that drive these trends.
the design of robust monitoring strategies for detecting population changes in the presence of uncertainty.
the design and implementation of monitoring programmes that can detect changes in population size and structure in the presence of uncertainty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
‘The effectiveness of a monitoring programme to detect population change is dependent on the budget, observation error, and the underlying processes that are being detected.’
monitoring should not be conducted if the cost of conducting the monitoring is more than the value of the information obtained.
the monitoring programme should be designed with the specific objectives in mind.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best monitoring strategy is to monitor frequently and to do so for a long time.
it is important that monitoring is done well, that is, with high-quality methods, and that it is done often enough to be able to detect trends, even if they are small.
it is important for monitoring programmes to be designed with the ecological processes to be detected, and the ecological conditions in which they will occur, in mind.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effectiveness of a monitoring programme depends on the underlying processes that are being monitored and the monitoring design.
robustness of monitoring depends not just on the budget, but also on how the budget is allocated over space, time and effort.
monitoring programmes need to be designed with the threats to detect in mind.
